Unnamed: 1: How the attrition label was built

Snapshot date is 30 September 2025. Features describe each employee at that date (tenure, pay position, raises, engagement, attendance, overtime, manager changes ...). The label left_within_12m is 1 if the employee left between 1 October 2025 and 30 September 2026. The extension rows follow the same rules so that you have enough data to train on. Split your data with care: use stratified folds and never let any information from after the snapshot into the features.
•  Protected attributes (gender, age) are deliberately kept in the separate sheets protected_attributes and resume_protected_attrs. Use them to TEST fairness, not as model inputs.

•  Labels for anomalies are in separate sheets (attendance_anomaly_labels, payroll_anomaly_labels). Treat them as hidden when you train an unsupervised detector, and use them only to measure catch rate.
•  The sample_* sheets show the output format a downstream dashboard expects (risk bands, reason codes, forecast ranges). They come from simple baseline models and are examples, not targets to copy.
•  baseline_benchmarks shows what honest models score. If your model scores far above that, check for leakage before celebrating.
•  The sheet answer_key_planted_dirt lists every planted data problem. Do your own audit first (Task 1), then compare.
•  Facts about the planted traps and how the data was built are summarised in the sheet answer_key_notes. Open it only after your own audit.
